art.subject: Bar-headed Goose (Anser indicus), adult: head white with two black horseshoe-shaped bars across the rear crown and nape; a white stripe running down each side of the neck; foreneck and hindneck dark grey; body pale silvery grey with darker grey flanks; back pale grey with pale feather fringes; rump and undertail white; tail grey with a white tip. Bill yellow-orange with a black nail; dark eye; legs and feet orange-yellow.
art.pose: standing on a grassy bank among other geese, side view
art.scene: Korean winter wetland beside harvested rice fields with grey geese; no people, buildings or text
views: adult (sexes alike), standing on a grassy bank, side view: white head with two black bars across the rear crown and nape, white stripe down each side of the dark grey-brown neck, orange-yellow bill, very pale grey body with darker grey flanks and pale feather fringes on the back, white undertail, orange-yellow legs

adult, swimming, three-quarter front view: white face and head with two black bars on the back of the head, dark foreneck with a white stripe down each side, orange-yellow bill, very pale grey breast and body
art.build: Medium-sized grey goose, a little smaller than Bean Goose and similar in size to Greater White-fronted Goose, but slimmer-necked and very pale. Bill shorter than the head, fairly slender, yellow-orange with a black nail. Legs medium length, orange-yellow. Tail short, rounded. In flight very pale grey wings with darker grey tips to the flight feathers and white uppertail coverts.
avoid: Do not paint the head grey-brown; it is white with two black bars at the back.
Do not paint a pink bill or pink legs (Greylag Goose); bill and legs are yellow-orange.
Do not paint a white forehead blaze or black belly bars (Greater White-fronted Goose).
Do not paint a black neck with a white chinstrap (Canada Goose).
